raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

`FlexAttentionImpl` re-derived its K/V cache views from the `kv_cache` tensor on
every call: the transpose/split in `do_kv_cache_update`, and the transpose/split
plus the flatten in the decoder `forward` path. These views depend only on the
`kv_cache` tensor storage/shape/strides, which are fixed once the cache is
allocated, so deriving them per call is pure host overhead on the eager critical
path and multiplies by `num_layers` per step.

Cache the derived views per `kv_cache` tensor identity, mirroring the
FlashAttention fix in #64571: `_get_kv_views` keyed on the tensor, rebuilt when
the profiling cache is replaced by the real one, and cleared in both
`_cleanup_profiling_kv_cache` and `clear_layer_kv_caches` via the
`_kv_view_cache` attribute convention so the profiling buffer is not pinned.

This addresses the `flex_attention.py` backend of #64572. The `_kv_view_cache`
teardown hunks share the attribute-name convention introduced by #64571;
whichever lands first makes the other a trivial rebase.

Related: #59534, #64571, #64572

## Testing

`pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flex_kv_view_cache.py` — 5 passed (CPU-only):
cache hit returns identical view objects, views match the direct derivation and
flatten to the expected shape, the cache rebuilds when the tensor is replaced,
teardown clears it, and an in-place write through the cached view aliases the
underlying `kv_cache` storage.

Host time per forward-path derivation vs a cached-view hit (CPU, N=4000 after
warmup, blocks=1000/block=16/kv_heads=4/head=128): **7.95 µs → 0.13 µs/call**.
`pre-commit` clean (ruff, ruff-format, mypy).

## Duplicate check

`gh pr list --state open --search "flex_attention kv view ..."`: no open PR
caches the Flex KV views. Triton (#64890) and `hpc_attn` (claimed by another
contributor) are the other #64572 backends; this PR is the `flex_attention.py`
one only.

---
I used an AI coding assistant to help investigate and implement this change; I
reviewed and verified it (tests + microbench + pre-commit above) and take
responsibility for the contents.

@@ -0,0 +1,97 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""CPU-only regression tests for the FlexAttention K/V view cache (#64572).
+
+Run `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flex_kv_view_cache.py`.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.flex_attention import FlexAttentionImpl
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test
+
+HEAD_SIZE = 128
+NUM_KV_HEADS = 4
+NUM_BLOCKS = 10
+BLOCK_SIZE = 16
+
+
+def _make_impl() -> FlexAttentionImpl:
+    return FlexAttentionImpl(
+        num_heads=8,
+        head_size=HEAD_SIZE,
+        scale=1.0,
+        num_kv_heads=NUM_KV_HEADS,
+        alibi_slopes=None,
+        sliding_window=None,
+        kv_cache_dtype="auto",
+    )
+
+
+def _make_kv_cache() -> torch.Tensor:
+    # Flex uses the LBNHC layout: the per-layer cache is stored so that
+    # transpose(1, 2) yields a contiguous [num_blocks, block_size, heads,
+    # 2 * head_size], which is what makes the forward-path flatten a zero-copy
+    # view. Build it the same way: a contiguous base seen transposed, exactly
+    # the tensor the model runner hands the impl.
+    base = torch.randn(NUM_BLOCKS, BLOCK_SIZE, NUM_KV_HEADS, 2 * HEAD_SIZE)
+    return base.transpose(1, 2)
+
+
+def test_views_are_cached_per_tensor_identity():
+    impl = _make_impl()
+    kv = _make_kv_cache()
+    k1, v1 = impl._get_kv_views(kv, flatten=False)
+    k2, v2 = impl._get_kv_views(kv, flatten=False)
+    # Same tensor in -> identical view objects back (no re-derivation).
+    assert k1 is k2 and v1 is v2
+    kf1, vf1 = impl._get_kv_views(kv, flatten=True)
+    kf2, vf2 = impl._get_kv_views(kv, flatten=True)
+    assert kf1 is kf2 and vf1 is vf2
+
+
+def test_views_match_direct_derivation():
+    impl = _make_impl()
+    kv = _make_kv_cache()
+    k_split, v_split = impl._get_kv_views(kv, flatten=False)
+    dk, dv = kv.transpose(1, 2).split(HEAD_SIZE, dim=-1)
+    assert torch.equal(k_split, dk) and torch.equal(v_split, dv)
+    k_flat, v_flat = impl._get_kv_views(kv, flatten=True)
+    assert k_flat.shape == (NUM_BLOCKS * BLOCK_SIZE, NUM_KV_HEADS, HEAD_SIZE)
+    assert torch.equal(k_flat, dk.reshape(-1, NUM_KV_HEADS, HEAD_SIZE))
+
+
+def test_cache_rebuilds_when_tensor_replaced():
+    impl = _make_impl()
+    kv_profiling = _make_kv_cache()
+    k_old, _ = impl._get_kv_views(kv_profiling, flatten=False)
+    # Real cache replaces the profiling one -> identity differs -> rebuild.
+    kv_real = _make_kv_cache()
+    k_new, _ = impl._get_kv_views(kv_real, flatten=False)
+    assert k_new is not k_old
+    assert impl._kv_view_cache is not None
+    assert impl._kv_view_cache[0] is kv_real
+
+
+def test_teardown_clears_cache():
+    impl = _make_impl()
+    kv = _make_kv_cache()
+    impl._get_kv_views(kv, flatten=False)
+    assert impl._kv_view_cache is not None
+    # Simulate _cleanup_profiling_kv_cache / clear_layer_kv_caches.
+    impl._kv_view_cache = None
+    k, _ = impl._get_kv_views(kv, flatten=False)
+    assert impl._kv_view_cache is not None
+
+
+def test_cached_view_aliases_storage():
+    impl = _make_impl()
+    kv = _make_kv_cache()
+    k_split, _ = impl._get_kv_views(kv, flatten=False)
+    # An in-place write through the cached view must land in kv (shared storage),
+    # so the attention kernels still read/write the real cache.
+    k_split.zero_()
+    dk, _ = kv.transpose(1, 2).split(HEAD_SIZE, dim=-1)
+    assert torch.all(dk == 0)

+        # Cache of the derived K/V cache views, keyed on the kv_cache tensor
+        # identity. See _get_kv_views and issue #64572 / #59534.

         """View a 3d tensor as 4D."""
@@ -1218,6 +1231,32 @@ def view_as_4d(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
         assert tensor.ndim == 3
         return tensor[None, :, :, :]
 
+    def _get_kv_views(
+        self, kv_cache: torch.Tensor, flatten: bool
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        # The K/V cache views depend only on kv_cache's storage, shape and
+        # strides, all fixed once the cache is allocated. Deriving them on every
+        # attention call (the transpose/split, plus the forward-path flatten) is
+        # pure host overhead on the eager critical path. Cache the views per
+        # kv_cache tensor identity and reuse them while the same tensor is passed
+        # in (issue #64572, mirrors the FlashAttention fix #64571).
+        #
+        # The identity check is required: profiling first binds a minimal KV
+        # cache, runs attention on it, frees it, then allocates the real one.
+        # Keying on identity rebuilds the views when the tensor is replaced, so
+        # the cache never points at freed memory.
+        cache = self._kv_view_cache
+        if cache is None or cache[0] is not kv_cache:
+            # (B, H, N, 2*hs) -> ((B, N, H, hs), (B, N, H, hs))
+            k_split, v_split = kv_cache.transpose(1, 2).split(self.head_size, dim=-1)
+            # Flatten (num_blocks, block_size) into a single token dim.
+            k_flat = k_split.view(-1, self.num_kv_heads, self.head_size)
+            v_flat = v_split.view(-1, self.num_kv_heads, self.head_size)
+            cache = self._kv_view_cache = (kv_cache, k_split, v_split, k_flat, v_flat)
+        if flatten:
+            return cache[3], cache[4]
+        return cache[1], cache[2]
